findings.reason: the author would cite these four owners and either extend the bounded-log helper or state plainly why §4's keep-head-and-tail policy cannot be built from the existing rotation and `line_boundary` primitives instead of re-deriving them.
findings.text: §4's per-run-file size bound (`gc.run_file_max_mb`, keeping first and last megabyte around a size-and-sha256 marker) duplicates bounded-log machinery the repository already owns and the plan does not cite, at these sites: the service-log bound `reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py:223` (`SERVICE_LOG_LIMIT_BYTES`/`SERVICE_LOG_KEEP_BYTES`, truncation at `fleet_supervisor.py:540-574`); the rotating watch-log stream `reckon/crew/runs.py:3985` (`WATCH_LOG_MAX_BYTES`, `_open` at `runs.py:4005`); the shared line-boundary helper `reckon/crew/runs.py:1923` (`line_boundary`) that any keep-head-and-tail cut needs; and, for "a file a ledger row names as a gate log", the declared-path extractor `reckon/crew/promotion_release.py:127` (`_declared_arm_paths`, `_ARM_LOG_FIELDS` at `promotion_release.py:56`, mirrored at `reckon/crew/promotion_records.py:258`)

findings.reason: adding the two-line "searched X and Y, rejected because Z" note §4 is missing would let the author reconcile the new policy with `WATCH_LOG_MAX_BYTES` and `SERVICE_LOG_LIMIT_BYTES` before implementation.
findings.text: §4 introduces a new run-file size-bounding mechanism without a reuse map over the codebase for it, unlike §2/§3/§5 which each name the mechanism they extend; because the two existing bounded-log sites named above are unlisted, a reader cannot tell whether the new policy is a deliberate divergence from rotation-by-newest or an oversight

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan hides substantial behaviour behind one interface: `crew gc` reports and, with `--apply`, acts, and each new store is a row set on `garbage_collect` (`reckon/crew/routing.py:1520`) rather than a new module, so the surface does not grow with the behaviour.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §4 re-implements a bounded-log store and a declared-path extractor whose owners already exist; the finding below names each.
rubric_items.interface_budget: public_definitions 1626, cli_options 351, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23 — pass: no section adds a CLI option (all reuse the existing `--apply`), an MCP view or a refusal family, and §3 retires surface rather than adding it by folding the plan-review raw-report sweep (`reckon/crew/routing.py:1431`) into the report row set.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan searched and cites the owners it extends for the ledger index (`reckon/ledger.py:896`), the gc sweep (`reckon/crew/routing.py:1520`), the pointer lock (`reckon/crew/runs.py:549`) and the pick-input cache root (`reckon/capabilities.py:1177`), but §4 adds a run-file size bound and a declared-gate-log lookup without citing the two mechanisms that already do those jobs.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — no section adds a pass-through layer: §2 records the indexed ledger path in the index's own `metadata` table (which already exists at `reckon/ledger.py:1104`), §3 extends the existing `garbage_collect` row-set pattern, and §4 says why the file is truncated rather than deleted, so each change extends an owner instead of wrapping it.
